messages:
claire-recruiter: Heads-up: After running the bulk candidate import this morning, some interviews show the wrong interviewer assigned in the ATS UI (e.g., Sophie listed but calendar shows Malik). Not all rows are affected. Anyone else seeing assignment drift?

nate-peopleops: Ugh. We had a smaller import last week that was fine. What format did you use for interviewer columns?

claire-recruiter: CSV from Greenhouse export. Columns: candidate_id, role, interviewer_email, interviewer_slot. I used the new bulk-import script `tools/ats_bulk_import.py` on prod.

lucy-ics: Can you paste a sample row (redact PII)? Also, are we seeing duplicated interview records or just mismatched user mapping?

claire-recruiter: Sample row: `12345, Backend Engineer, sophie@redwood.ai, 2026-04-02T14:00Z` but in ATS the interviewer attached is `malik@redwood.ai`. There are ~12 mismatches across 3 roles.

evan-ild-bot: Import validator: mismatch rate 0.7% (12/1700). Flag: ambiguous email alias mapping for users with same display name. Logs: user_map_lookup returned multiple matches for 'Sophie Chen' id=user_lookup_ambig_77.

ryan-hiring-mgr: We recently onboarded two Sophies (Sophie Chen and Sophie Li) in the Eng org. Could be alias collision. The CSV had `sophie@redwood.ai` which should map to Sophie Chen. Curious why Malik got mapped.

nate-peopleops: Malik has a display name 'M. Chen' in the directory and shares the same last name as Sophie Chen. Might be a heuristic in the lookup that favors last-name matches when emails are missing or normalized.

lucy-ics: Ops ask: were any rows missing interviewer_email and using display names instead? Those are risky.

claire-recruiter: No, all rows had emails. But I did run a normalization step that lowercased and trimmed whitespace. No other transforms.

evan-ild-bot: Found root cause: bulk-import fallback logic uses secondary lookup when primary email-to-user lookup returns >1 or 0 results. Secondary heuristic uses last_name + team alias. In this import, Sophie Chen had a stale team tag in directory (listed under "infra") and Malik's account had a legacy alias 's.chen@' in our AD which matched loosely. So heuristic picked Malik.

nate-peopleops: Noted. Immediate fix: revert heuristic to strict email-only mapping for bulk imports and surface ambiguous rows to a review queue instead of best-effort assign. Can we patch quickly?

ops-bot: Runbook proposal: 1) Pause remaining bulk imports, 2) Re-run importer with strict email mapping for yesterday's job, 3) Create review queue for ambiguous rows, 4) Notify affected candidate owners and interviewers.

lucy-ics: I'll pause the scheduled imports. Claire, can you send the list of affected candidate IDs? I'll coordinate calendar corrections and notify interviewers.

claire-recruiter: Sent DM with IDs (redacted here). Also, can we add a preflight check to the tool that ensures every `interviewer_email` exists uniquely in directory and fails the import with a CSV of ambiguous entries?

nate-peopleops: Agree. I'll add a validation step and a `--dry-run` flag to the import script. Also will write a short KB note for recruiters about not editing AD aliases during onboarding.

evan-ild-bot: Patch proposed on branch `hotfix/import-strict-email` with tests. ETA for production patch 2 hours.

ryan-hiring-mgr: Thanks all. Requesting follow-up in the thread once calendars are corrected so I can update candidates.

ops-bot: Incident status: mitigation in progress. Reopen if mismatches persist after reimport. :white_check_mark:
